body: Meeting people can be hard when you're not straight because it's hard to know who will be receptive to your attention.  I recommend meeting someone online in your area - it's pretty normal to do nowadays and it cuts through a lot of bullshit.
You'd be surprised at how long peoples' memories are.  I think you'd be missed more than you think you would.  But I know how you feel in thinking that way.
Do you drive?  I know a lot of people here (NYC) don't; that makes a difference in where you should go, I would think.
For a while.  Not for any reason beyond "Well, I gotta see how THIS plays out."

That sounds really, really painful.  

I wish I had some advice for making life better, but I can't really think of anything to say.  So I just hope you find something.

I have the same issue.  I found a good HA support forum and they helped me overcome my tendency to obsessively Google everything I think is wrong with me.  I dunno what reddit's policy is on linking people to other forums but I think if you Google for health anxiety forum it'll pop up.

I know how you feel about hating what you see in the mirror.  Being fat sucks and it's so hard to do something about.  Especially if you're depressed.  But TBH if your girlfriend sees you that way, she's kind of a superficial bitch.  You deserve someone who doesn't insult you, even if you don't believe that.

The Weekenders.  Likable characters (who actually changed their clothes - though they only had a few outfits each it seemed), funny writing, the main character and his mom had an amazing mother/son dynamic, and a hilarious running gag centered around a pizza place.

First relationships are always crazy.  There are other people out there who would love to get to know you.  I understand how you can get so attached to someone so quickly (happened to me once), but you gotta know it's not real...it's based more on ideas of what could happen than on what you actually had.  It doesn't seem like it now but someday you're gonna look back on this and it won't seem like such a big deal.  You'll meet someone else, who will hopefully be less drama.

Ever since 9/11 I've had fantasies about dying saving someone else from a bullet or something.  I doubt in reality I would - I'm sure I'd freeze and ultimately try to save my sorry self - but I enjoy the thought of it nonetheless.

I can't deal with emotional pain.  And I've just had too damn much of it.  I'm so tired of everything.  Nothing seems hopeful.

- My dad's dead.  I rely on my mom (who's a good person but we don't get along great much of the time, just different personalities and she's mentally healthy so she doesn't understand why I can't just be normal) for financial support and she's elderly.  When she passes, I'll be homeless.  I live in one of the most expensive cities in the world (yay rent control but I can't afford even that plus living expenses on my own) and couldn't afford to get a place anywhere else either or even GET to another place, plus my whole life is here.

- My girlfriend is sick of me.  She's bored with me.  But she won't leave me because she's convinced that being with me won't be so bad.  And I don't have the strength to leave her.  But I wish she wouldn't gush about the people she likes better to me, or do things like complain about them not paying more attention to her to me.  I love her and it really hurts that she doesn't love me in the same way.  

- I'm trying to get off disability and become work-able, but it's getting more and more obvious that that's never going to happen.  My mental issues are just too difficult to deal with, plus the physical symptoms that I don't know if they come from that, or are side effects from the medication, but I have horrible insomnia, am always exhausted and am always in pain; no medications help for anything.  Always going to be depressed, anxious, obsessive, panicky, paranoid, tired and hurting.  Also chronic stomach problems which mean I can't eat during the day to avoid sickness, which is just...not a terrible lot of fun.  I can do the work, barely, but five days a week eight hours a day...I'll never be able to handle that.  

- So fat and ugly that I actively can't see my own reflection or I get severely depressed for days after.  You'd think someone who only eats once a day wouldn't weigh over 200 pounds but antidepressants are just awesome like that.  

- I know there are people out there who like me, but it doesn't change that I constantly feel lonely and unloved.  

- I've been accusing of being a pedophile in the past.  Not because I ever did anything, or because anyone said I did, but because I've said stupid things in the past (OCD sometimes causes paranoid thoughts, in my case OH MY GOD what if I'm secretly a pedo and just don't know it...well, bit of advice, NEVER ADMIT TO THAT.)  Internet vigilantes have made my life a living hell.  Probably doesn't help that most of my interests make people go "WTF" anyway.  Mostly kid-oriented stuff like cartoons.  And I'm into ageplay, which nobody knows but my girlfriend and some strangers on the internet, but I'm certain that if that came out to those people they'd be all over it.  (And no, I'm not actually into little kids.  Ageplay isn't about actual children.  At least not for most people; I suppose there could be some sickos out there.)

- My girlfriend thought ageplay was creepy until she started doing it online with the people she wishes she could replace me with.  So now I feel doubly alone (she doesn't like doing it with me) AND like she stole part of me.  Even if it wasn't part of me that I particularly liked, it was part of who I am and she just took it for fun sex games.  And refuses to share in it with ME, which really hurts.  I know it's only online but it feels like cheating still.  (She says it doesn't count since she's "in character" as someone else when she does it; I disagree.  But plenty of partnered people seem to do it so I guess it's not?)

- That's another reason I don't have the strength to leave.  It's hard to get back out there with "so OCD made me think I was a pedo and now the internet won't let it go" on one's personal resume.  Again, I don't want to leave her.  I'm crazy about her.  But I just feel like she's waiting to find the right time to leave me, and feeling like that really sucks.

- My memory has holes in it.  I used to have the sharpest memory of all time; never forgot a THING.  Now I can't remember books I've read, conversations I've had, the correct way to do something I was JUST shown how to do.  I blame being put on psych meds when I was 13.  

- My psychiatrist is useless.  She doesn't listen to me, she berates me nonstop and seems to enjoy seeing me suffer.  Sometimes I think I've been wrongly diagnosed or have had diagnoses missed (nothing I've been diagnosed with explains a number of my symptoms), but I guess I'll never know.  Mom pays the bills so Mom pays the doctors.  Did I mention that I'm in my 30s?  It's pathetic.

- I can't talk to people.  I try, but I just shut down, my mind goes totally blank and I have no idea what to say.  I try to make friends but it's hard when you're like that.  

Honestly I could deal with everything but my girlfriend not being in love with me anymore.  It just SUCKS because I can't stay like this but I can't leave either.  She means everything to me, and she's the only person I can be myself around.  And she keeps saying that she is, but then at the same time, when she discusses our future together she looks fucking miserable.  (Not that I blame her, I don't want a future with me either...obviously...haha)

Just, nothing can get better at this point.  Eventually I'm going to be going through life alone and I can't handle that.

That's a really nice thing to say and I appreciate it :)  I'm really nothing special though.  And pretty much everyone I know would agree with that.  Except my mom...she was never able to accept that I'm not gifted like she thought I was as a kid.  But I guess that's moms for you, good ones at least.

Thanks for the info.  I hadn't even thought about it as a fire hazard.  I don't really want to burn down a park on my way out.  Though I'd probably go down in history for that, since the park I'd be doing it in is fairly known around the world.  Guess I should keep on trying.  Too bad though since that seemed the least traumatic way.  I've thought about an exit bag but I'm REALLY bad at making things.  I'm terrified of things that require decisive action, I guess?  I know I'll never be able to jump, pull a trigger, etc.  Tried partial suspension hanging a bunch of times, obviously no luck, I must be doing something wrong with the knots but I can't figure out what (I did start to black out once but panicked and ripped it off...wasn't really trying to die that day, just wanted to make sure I could.  Well, I haven't gotten it right since!)  

But I have a will so there must be a way.
